chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb and 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, said: We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about a man who sold food for dirhams for a specified term. When the term arrived, he demanded payment, and the seller said to him, 'I do not have dirhams with me; take food from me.' He (the Imam) said, 'There is no harm in it; he only has his dirhams, and he may take whatever he wishes with them.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Can a debtor repay a monetary debt with goods instead of cash?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the creditor is granted the autonomy to accept goods in lieu of cash debt, reflecting the principle that the creditor holds the right to choose the form of settlement. This highlights the flexibility in Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding debt liquidation, distinguishing between the obligation to pay and the specific medium of payment. The ruling underscores the creditor's discretion to convert the monetary claim into tangible assets, provided both parties agree to the substitution.
